feature: N09: the default single-plugin product runs one managed Task Service over the same SQLite authority, with unified Bot/account admission, durable cancel/retry/reconciliation, and a managed CLI backend gated on a host-verified official entry

changes.taskServiceWiring: The composition boot opens the Task journal on the same orchestration.sqlite, creates one Task Service whose execution context is the shared policy, registers the bounded bot_task_* tools and releases them on dispose or a failed boot. A previous Host that died without releasing its runner lease blocks the claim until it expires, so the next boot waits instead of dropping every managed task
changes.backendDecision: Resolved queue decision point 2: the durable target contract stays fixed per backend kind (mr-api, codex-read) while the execution target, model and money resolve at run time from the submitting Bot's committed binding. A binding change therefore never rewrites a persisted target hash, retries of older tasks stay admissible, and each Bot is charged at its own configured price. The binding is the single source of truth for grant and money, so no service-level model check is duplicated
changes.cliEntryGate: The CLI backend exists only when the host declares an installation-verified entry (executable, sha256, version) plus verified CLI model identities; neither a Bot nor a Task input can supply an entry. Without configuration the catalog exposes no codex tool, modes or cliModels, so a Bot binding cannot select an unverified CLI identity
changes.readModelAndActions: The tasks read-model section pages the durable journal per Bot with the available backend catalog, and owner task.cancel/retry/reconcile actions run on the owning Bot's own subject so the Bot's committed grant authorizes every operation
changes.catalog: The settings catalog adds the managed-tasks capability (task tools plus the MR execution capabilities), the codex official-tool entry with its CLI grant tools, and the task backend catalog; the compiled grant takes its tools from the selected capabilities
changes.unknownReceiptResolution: The owner action usage.resolve settles an unconfirmed package in one CAS transaction: it attests a vendor-confirmed amount or waives it, releases the interrupted execution hold that keeps its estimate and unknown count, and records the resolution on the run so the commit digest chain is the audit trail. The usage read model exposes the resolvable packages and each receipt resolution; a cross-Bot attempt is refused by ownership before any state changes.
changes.reviewUi: The usage page renders the reviewable unconfirmed packages as cards with a required note, an optional vendor-confirmed amount and two gated actions (attest the confirmed amount, or waive with the note), and each receipt row shows its resolution tag; the shipped bundle is rebuilt and verified.
changes.taskConcurrency: The Task Service accepts a per-Bot concurrency limit and the composition passes the committed binding maxConcurrentTasks. The durable target contract stays per backend kind, so a concurrency change never rewrites a persisted target hash; an unconfigured Bot, or any answer outside the stored 1..32 range, keeps the conservative single-task default instead of failing open.

fixes: The composition used dirname without importing it, so the product host aborted before any service opened

The probe drove reconciliation through the Bot's own AgentLoop, but an unconfirmed receipt fail-closes that Bot's model turns; recovery now runs through the real owner action on the owning Bot's subject

The receipts-versus-summary invariant counted an unconfirmed receipt's usage in both sides; the confirmed receipts now reconcile with the spend total and the unconfirmed amount is asserted separately as unknown

A duplicate resolution attempt by another Bot was reported as an ownership refusal rather than a duplicate; the probe now asserts both the cross-Bot ownership refusal and the same-Bot duplicate refusal
remoteMachineEvidence: Ubuntu and Win10 re-runs of the default composition probe are pending; this checkpoint was produced on the local Win11 machine only
limitations: The managed CLI backend runs on a contract-level fixture session factory declared by the probe; no native codex executable is spawned and the real entry still needs an install-verified host decision (local codex-cli 0.157.1 cannot initialize its sqlite state in an isolated home)
The CLI facade admits through its own budget reservation plus the Bot grant; one shared Task/outbox admission transaction with the funding authority is still open
An evicted run folds its unknown into the archive and is no longer individually resolvable; the review must happen while the run is retained
No default user profile migration, Electron carrier, clean install, three-machine re-run or real model inference

The review UI is verified for rendering and gating; typing is not simulated in the jsdom harness because React is imported before the DOM is installed, so the resolve payload semantics stay covered by the real-host probe and the native suite
